name: Criminal force and violence against the person
description: Legal constructs governing assault, battery, homicide, and related offenses—where the state punishes unjustified injury or credible threats, often discussed alongside moral critiques of wrath and disproportionate anger.
foundationStrengthRationale: Core of penal law everywhere; self-defense and proportionality doctrines differ by system.

pros.claim: Protects bodily integrity and public order through clear prohibitions on unlawful harm.
pros.evidence: Battery and assault statutes and common-law crimes form a stable cross-jurisdictional family.

cons.claim: Legal 'force' doctrines do not track spiritual 'wrath' perfectly; justified force and systemic violence raise separate questions.
cons.evidence: Policing, war, and self-defense carve out large exceptions that moral theology treats under different headings.
